◌ Planetary orbits · 3D ellipses JPL model

Each planet follows its own elliptical orbit, oriented in three dimensions. Bodies travel faster near the Sun and slower farther away. Select a planet to view its orbit measurements in Data & Evidence.

Scale: Planetary spacing and sizes are still deliberately compressed or enlarged in these scenes; inclination at 1× and each orbit's eccentricity retain their geometry within its display mapping. Higher inclination settings exaggerate height only.

JPL approximation · years 1800–2050 preferred

Visual layers
◉ Rotation axes, orbital paths & orientation

IAU/JPL spin poles remain fixed in their inertial frame as planets orbit. Venus and Uranus rotate retrograde. Saturn/Uranus rings use the same equatorial plane as each planet. Planetary radii are deliberately enlarged; magnetic/plasma boundaries are separate, Sun-facing systems.

Blue = polar axis · gold arrow = sense of spin · purple = illustrative magnetic axis. Choose a planet to inspect orientation and source.

⌁ Spacetime & Gravity
1.0×
◈ WORLD-ANCHORED GRAVITY · v24.6D.8

Field fixed to its astronomical frame · camera movement changes projection only.

Changing zoom or orbit never changes the field's source positions, radius or intrinsic depth. Display radius and masses are simplified unless in the Sun/Earth calculated Newtonian mode. Local view selects the nearest modelled mass.

Relative potential surfaceEquipotential / attraction

Shown: an illustrative two-dimensional slice of a softened gravitational potential, projected into a 3D display. Local weights, distances and depth are deliberately normalised for readability. This is not a photograph of spacetime, an Einstein-equation solution, a gravitational-wave signal or a dark-matter measurement.

Science reference: NASA — understanding the spacetime fabric analogy ↗

v0.22 · GRAVITY PHYSICS

The original deformed-grid illustration remains available unchanged.

Use the original controls above to change the well, contours, vectors and field-direction paths. These are analogies, not the geometry of four-dimensional space-time.

Physics initialising

What is physical? Newtonian acceleration, potential and test-probe motion use JPL gravitational parameters (km³/s²), kilometres and seconds. Integration uses velocity Verlet. The separately mapped mint-green orbit is drawn within the existing exaggerated 3D scene. The displayed planets now use the selected orbital-geometry model, while the gravity probe remains a separate experiment and the 3D warped well remains illustrative.

The moving Earth/Moon secondary, when enabled, is prescribed as a circle; its gravitational feedback and other bodies are omitted. These are educational initial conditions, not real-time ephemerides, relativistic geodesics, gravitational lensing or full N-body predictions.

JPL masses: Astrodynamic Parameters ↗. The Horizons system ↗ is a future ephemeris-integration reference.

✦ Dynamic visual effects

Object locator = navigation aid. Solar-wind and auroral motion = schematic physical processes, not observed event forecasts. Galaxy glints = visual contrast only. Web highlights = conceptual and never measured galaxy or matter velocities.

◈ Magnetic environments · evidence-checked

Schematic field shapes: not to the same scale as the orbit or planet. Inspector gives measured dayside distances in planetary radii; real boundaries change with solar-wind pressure. An induced interaction is not a global planetary dynamo.

◈ Observational survey · v0.21.1

Bundled 2MRS reference sample: 286 deterministically selected measurements from the published 43,533-redshift catalogue (a truncated, non-representative sample of qualifying entries). Original celestial coordinates and line-of-sight velocities are used; distances are only approximate cz/H₀ proxies. This is a deliberately small, non-complete subset and is not a density estimate.

The 2MRS velocity and cz/H₀ conversion are not direct distances. Distances from redshift are unreliable for nearby galaxies with large peculiar velocities. Nearby peculiar velocities and choice of reference frame matter. Imported markers are not stellar models or inferred filaments. No file is uploaded anywhere.

Bundled 2MRS sample ready; individual catalogue points available offline.

Scientific boundary: RA/Dec are catalogue directions; distances are heterogeneous published-reference estimates from a secondary curated compilation. 3D positions are spherical distance transforms, not an original redshift-survey reconstruction. No inferred filament links or dark-matter density claims are made from this limited sample. NASA 2MRS full-survey reference ↗

This subsection controls ONLY the illustrative layers. Reference-coordinate objects come from the separate catalogue controls above. Pulses are explanatory highlights, not matter or galaxy velocities. Time does not yet calculate cosmic-web evolution.

🌍 Earth Accuracy · NASA surface + WGS84 24.6D.5

Upgraded Earth surface: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation geography, bundled offline. WGS84 flattening and sidereal orientation are implemented in the WebGL Earth surface shader.

Earth surface texture: checking renderer.

Accuracy boundary: continents, coastlines and seasonal ice are mapped from a historic satellite composite; no live weather or clouds. The magnetosphere, auroral curtains, Sun position in the magnetic scene, field-line shape and observational epoch remain illustrative. Not a geomagnetic or meteorological forecast.

WGS84 equatorial radius: 6,378.137 km · polar radius: 6,356.752 km · axial tilt: 23.44° · sidereal day: 23.9345 h. Geographic north is independent of magnetic north.
